analysis:
Examined both ClusterControlLeadership.swift excerpts and ClusterOnboardingFlow.swift metadata, changed ranges and bounded patch. The leadership changes add an optional stop-generation value to forwarded serve requests (head 828–836), expose the leader's stop count in replies (869–871), and copy it into onboarding status (874–878). The visible Flow patch adds stop-count and guarded-serve callbacks (head 1518–1525); defaults retain previous behavior. These changes address provider availability and operator stop intent (A-018), not serving authorization. Existing claim ordering, lease confirmation, plan-bound solo admission and command routing were examined as surrounding context, but are not changed by this PR's supplied range map.
No concrete regression is established: these protocol fields do not themselves authorize serving, expose prompt/key material, alter cache isolation (T-041), or weaken attestation. Optional compatibility behavior is not proof of a deployed bypass. The material unresolved contract is end-to-end enforcement: integration must inspect ClusterOnboardingFlow.swift's other changed ranges (head 2901–3539), the live callback wiring and localServe implementation to verify that the count is captured before asynchronous work, forwarded without loss, and compared atomically with stop recording on the authoritative leader. Leadership changes during a start and unknown/nil counts also require reconciliation. The supplied Flow metadata and partial patch do not show those implementations; no finding is inferred from that coverage limit. Authorization/final admission (T-053), serving-lock/add-on hold interaction (T-059), and restart/watchdog behavior must remain authoritative when the new guarded serve path is used.
